native_result.query: In which century did summed social capital peak, what individual social capital components like gold, monument etc increase?
native_result.HypoA: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?
native_result.HypoB: Summed social capital (Copper&Gold + Amber + MonumentCount z-scores) peaked in the 14th century BCE (anchor BCE 1400 / CE -1400 / ~3350 calBP, data group OBA): capital.csv row BCE 1400 sums to 4.238 (2.540 - 0.010 + 1.708), identically confirmed by the interpolated time-series century bin CE -1400 (4.238). It sits atop a plateau (BCE 1300 tied; BCE 1200/1100 = 3.622 second). Rising components vs the preceding century (BCE 1500), ranked: Copper & Gold (+2.90, -0.36 to +2.54) > Monument Count (+1.54, +0.17 to +1.71) > Amber (marginal +0.14, -0.15 to -0.01; amber stays below its series mean). The peak is driven chiefly by copper/gold wealth and monumental construction (elite material display) in the OBA phase; amber contributes negligibly.
native_result.WorkflowB: Read 3 CSVs (fix decimal commas) -> define social = ZCU_AU+Zamber+ZMonument -> main: rank capital.csv century rows, peak BCE 1400 (4.238) -> cross-validate: time_series interpolated columns binned by CE//100*100, peak bin -1400 (4.238, MATCH) -> component criteria: main delta vs previous century; aux vs series mean; 5-century trajectory -> sensitivity: +1 extra indicator each and all-12 sum (peak 1400 robust for capital triad and all-12; shifts to 1100/1200/2700 when adding Depot/HouseSize/PotteryForm) -> reproducible script analysis_social_capital.py (executed).

sub_hypo.text: Summed social capital peaked at BCE 1400 in the OBA phase, with a sum of 4.238, identically confirmed by the interpolated time-series century bin CE -1400.
sub_hypo.context: Archaeological century rows and interpolated time-series century bins; OBA phase at BCE 1400 / CE -1400 / approximately 3350 calBP. Time-series bins are defined by CE//100*100.
sub_hypo.relations: Social capital is the additive sum of Copper & Gold, Amber, and Monument Count z-scores. At BCE 1400, 2.540 - 0.010 + 1.708 = 4.238, matching the interpolated century-bin sum at CE -1400.

sub_hypo.text: The social-capital peak sits atop a plateau: BCE 1300 ties BCE 1400, while BCE 1200 and 1100 tie for second at 3.622.
sub_hypo.context: Ranked archaeological century rows, specifically BCE 1400, 1300, 1200, and 1100.
sub_hypo.relations: The summed z-scores satisfy BCE 1400 = BCE 1300 = 4.238 > BCE 1200 = BCE 1100 = 3.622.

sub_hypo.text: The rise to the BCE 1400 peak was driven chiefly by copper/gold wealth and monumental construction, interpreted as elite material display in the OBA phase; amber contributed negligibly and remained below its series mean.
sub_hypo.context: OBA-phase peak at BCE 1400 compared with the preceding century, BCE 1500; component levels also assessed against their series means.
sub_hypo.relations: Component increases rank Copper & Gold (+2.90, from -0.36 to +2.54) > Monument Count (+1.54, from +0.17 to +1.71) > Amber (+0.14, from -0.15 to -0.01). Amber remains below its series mean.

sub_hypo.text: The BCE 1400 peak is robust for the social-capital triad and the all-12-indicator sum, but adding Depot, House Size, or Pottery Form individually shifts the peak to BCE 1100, 1200, or 2700, respectively.
sub_hypo.context: Sensitivity analysis of archaeological century rows, adding one indicator at a time to the social-capital triad and separately summing all 12 indicators.
sub_hypo.relations: Peak timing depends on indicator composition: the triad and all-12 sums peak at BCE 1400; triad + Depot peaks at BCE 1100, triad + House Size at BCE 1200, and triad + Pottery Form at BCE 2700.
